title: Lean & Strong
subtitle: 9-week home program · waistline focus
summary: 3 home workouts a week with dumbbells, a kettlebell and ankle weights, a waist circuit every session, and a walk every day.

summary.effort: Finish each set feeling you could do 3 more reps

summary.sets: 4 sets on pair A, 3 sets on B & C
4 sets on pairs A & B, 3 sets on C
summary.waistCircuit: 3 rounds, add 10 s to every hold

A.title: Workout A
A.intro: Your legs are your biggest muscles, so working them burns the most energy. Rows build the upper back that pulls your shoulders back and makes your waist look slimmer.

warmup.text: Skip rope (4, 5 or 6 rounds by phase) or walk briskly on the pad for 5 min, then 2–3 min of mobility.
warmup.alternative: 5 min brisk walk on the walking pad

A.restNote: Go straight from the 1st to the 2nd exercise of a pair, then rest **60 s** (weeks 1–3), **45–60 s** (weeks 4–6) or **45 s** (weeks 7–9). Finish all sets of a pair before moving on.

waistCircuit.title: Waist circuit
waistCircuit.description: Do the three moves back to back, rest 45–60 s, repeat: **2 rounds** (weeks 1–3), **3 rounds** (weeks 4–9, holds +10 s from week 7).

walkAfter.text: Walk after: 25 min (weeks 1–3), 30 min (weeks 4–6), 35–40 min (weeks 7–9) at a brisk pace.

notes: Goblet squat: hold the kettlebell by the horns, close to your chest, elbows pointing down.
Rows: pull your elbows towards your back pockets. When 5 kg feels easy, lower for a slow count of 3.
Knee push-ups are a real exercise, not a cheat. Move to full push-ups once you can do 12 good ones.

cooldown.text: Stretch for 3 min, 30 s per stretch. Hip-flexor stretches matter most for anyone who sits all day.

B.title: Workout B
B.intro: Kettlebell swings get your heart rate up fast, which makes this the sweatiest session of the week. The waist circuit trains your core from three angles.

warmup.text: Skip rope (4, 5 or 6 rounds by phase) or walk briskly on the pad for 5 min, then 2–3 min of mobility.
warmup.alternative: 5 min brisk walk on the walking pad

B.restNote: Go straight from the 1st to the 2nd exercise of a pair, then rest **60 s** (weeks 1–3), **45–60 s** (weeks 4–6) or **45 s** (weeks 7–9). Finish all sets of a pair before moving on.

waistCircuit.title: Waist circuit
waistCircuit.description: Do the three moves back to back, rest 45–60 s, repeat: **2 rounds** (weeks 1–3), **3 rounds** (weeks 4–9, holds +10 s from week 7).

walkAfter.text: Walk after: 25 min (weeks 1–3), 30 min (weeks 4–6), 35–40 min (weeks 7–9) at a brisk pace.

notes: Swings are a hip snap, not an arm lift. The kettlebell floats to chest height because your hips drive it.
Keep your lower back pressed into the mat during reverse crunches. Slow beats fast.
Ankle weights are for the leg raises and kickbacks only. Never walk in them; they strain your knees and hips.

cooldown.text: Stretch for 3 min, 30 s per stretch. Hip-flexor stretches matter most for anyone who sits all day.

C.title: Workout C
C.intro: A mix of A and B with extra glute work. Slow squats make a light kettlebell feel heavy, and that's the point. Finish the week with your longest walk if you have time.

warmup.text: Skip rope (4, 5 or 6 rounds by phase) or walk briskly on the pad for 5 min, then 2–3 min of mobility.
warmup.alternative: 5 min brisk walk on the walking pad

C.restNote: Go straight from the 1st to the 2nd exercise of a pair, then rest **60 s** (weeks 1–3), **45–60 s** (weeks 4–6) or **45 s** (weeks 7–9). Finish all sets of a pair before moving on.

waistCircuit.title: Waist circuit
waistCircuit.description: Do the three moves back to back, rest 45–60 s, repeat: **2 rounds** (weeks 1–3), **3 rounds** (weeks 4–9, holds +10 s from week 7).

walkAfter.text: Walk after: 25 min (weeks 1–3), 30 min (weeks 4–6), 35–40 min (weeks 7–9) at a brisk pace.

notes: Squeeze your glute at the top of every kickback and hold for a second.
On the woodchop, turn from your ribs and pivot your back foot. Keep your arms long.
Friday's walk is a good one to make longer: it sets up a strong weekend.

cooldown.text: Stretch for 3 min, 30 s per stretch. Hip-flexor stretches matter most for anyone who sits all day.

skipping.name: Skipping Rope
cues: Elbows close to your sides; turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
Small hops of 2–3 cm, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Breathe steadily and rest when your form breaks down.
skipping.watchOut: Big jumps or landing flat-footed. Sore knees or shins? Warm up with 5 min brisk walking instead.

walking_pad.name: Walking Pad Walk
cues: Stand tall, eyes forward, shoulders relaxed and arms swinging naturally.
Take short, quick steps and land under your hips, heel to toe.
Brisk pace: you can talk in short sentences but not sing.
walking_pad.watchOut: Looking down at your phone the whole time. Prop it at eye level, and never wear ankle weights while walking.

kb_goblet_squat.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
cues: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at your chest, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit down and back between your heels until your thighs are about parallel.
Drive up through your whole foot and squeeze your glutes at the top.
kb_goblet_squat.watchOut: Heels lifting or knees caving in. Keep your chest proud and the kettlebell close.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

db_bent_over_row.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, soften your knees and hinge forward with a flat back.
Pull both dumbbells to your hips, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
db_bent_over_row.watchOut: Rounding your back or standing up as you pull. Brace your stomach and keep the hinge.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

db_reverse_lunge.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
cues: Stand tall with a 5 kg dumbbell in each hand.
Step one foot back and lower your back knee towards the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand back up. Alternate legs.
db_reverse_lunge.watchOut: Leaning forward or your front knee caving in. Too wobbly? Skip the dumbbells and hold a wall.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

knee_push_up.name: Knee Push-Up
cues: Knees on the mat, hands just wider than shoulders, straight line from knees to head.
Lower until your chest is a fist from the floor, elbows about 45°.
Push the floor away back to straight arms.
knee_push_up.watchOut: Hips piking up or sagging. Too hard? Do them with your hands on the couch or a table.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3
Move to full push-ups at 12 good reps

kb_glute_bridge.name: Kettlebell Glute Bridge
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, kettlebell resting on your hip bones.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until you're straight from knees to shoulders.
Hold 2 s at the top, then lower slowly.
kb_glute_bridge.watchOut: Arching your lower back. Push through your heels and let the glutes do the work.

hammer_curl.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
cues: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
Curl up with your palms still facing in, elbows still.
Lower slowly, for a count of 3 when 5 kg gets easy.
hammer_curl.watchOut: Swinging your body to lift the weights.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

kb_swing.name: Kettlebell Swing
cues: Feet wider than hips, hinge and 'hike' the kettlebell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward hard and stand tall; let the bell float to chest height.
Let it fall back between your legs and hinge straight into the next rep.
kb_swing.watchOut: Squatting it or lifting with your arms. It's a hip hinge. Start with 10 reps if it feels new.

db_floor_press.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
cues: Lie on the mat, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand with elbows on the floor.
Press the dumbbells straight up over your chest.
Lower slowly until your upper arms touch the floor.
db_floor_press.watchOut: Bouncing your elbows off the floor. Pause for a second there instead.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

kb_rdl.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Stand tall holding the kettlebell in both hands in front of your thighs, knees soft.
Push your hips back and slide the bell down your legs to just below the knees.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall.
kb_rdl.watchOut: Rounding your back. The stretch belongs in the back of your legs.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

db_shoulder_press.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
cues: Sit tall on a sturdy chair, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press up until your arms are straight and the dumbbells nearly touch.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
db_shoulder_press.watchOut: Arching your lower back. Brace your stomach as if someone might poke it.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

side_lying_leg_raise.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
cues: Ankle weights on, lie on your side with your head resting on your lower arm.
Lift the top leg up to about 45°, toes pointing forward, not up.
Lower slowly. Do all reps, then switch sides.
side_lying_leg_raise.watchOut: Rolling your hips backwards. Stack your hips and keep the movement small and slow.

overhead_triceps_ext.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
cues: Sit tall on a chair and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Lower it behind your head by bending your elbows; keep your elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms back to the top.
overhead_triceps_ext.watchOut: Elbows flaring wide or your lower back arching.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

glute_kickback.name: Glute Kickback
cues: Ankle weights on, start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keeping the knee bent, push your heel up towards the ceiling.
Squeeze at the top for a second, then lower. Do all reps, then switch legs.
glute_kickback.watchOut: Arching your back to kick higher. Stop when your thigh is level with your body.

options: Squeeze and pause 2 s at the top

dead_bug.name: Dead Bug
cues: Lie on your back, arms up and knees bent at 90° over your hips.
Press your lower back into the mat, then slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg.
Return and switch sides. Breathe out as you reach.
dead_bug.watchOut: Your lower back lifting off the mat. Only go as low as you can keep it flat.

plank.name: Forearm Plank
cues: Elbows under your shoulders, forearms on the mat.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button in: straight line from head to heels.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time.
plank.watchOut: Hips sagging or piking up. Can't hold good form? Drop to your knees (right picture).

side_plank.name: Side Plank
cues: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, feet stacked.
Lift your hips until your body is a straight line from head to feet.
Hold, breathing slowly, then switch sides.
side_plank.watchOut: Hips sagging towards the floor. Start with knees bent (right picture) and build up.

reverse_crunch.name: Reverse Crunch
cues: Lie on your back, arms by your sides, knees bent at 90° over your hips.
Curl your knees towards your chest, lifting your hips a few centimetres off the mat.
Lower slowly back to 90°.
reverse_crunch.watchOut: Swinging your legs to build momentum. Small and controlled works the abs.

options: Lower for a slow count of 3

bird_dog.name: Bird Dog
cues: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Hold 2 s, return and switch sides.
bird_dog.watchOut: Twisting your hips. Imagine a glass of water balanced on your lower back.

mountain_climber.name: Mountain Climber
cues: Start in the top of a push-up, hands under your shoulders.
Drive one knee towards your chest, then quickly switch legs.
Keep your hips level and keep moving for the set time.
mountain_climber.watchOut: Hips bouncing high. Slow it down or step the feet in rather than lose form.

woodchop.name: Standing Dumbbell Woodchop
cues: Feet wide, hold one dumbbell in both hands above one shoulder.
Chop it diagonally across your body down to the outside of the opposite knee.
Turn from your ribs and pivot your back foot. Do all reps, then switch sides.
woodchop.watchOut: Bending only your arms. The turn should come from your waist and hips.

sections.body: Three home workouts a week, a walk every day, and the calorie counting you're already doing. Strength work keeps your muscle while you lose fat, the waist circuit trains the muscles that hold your middle in, and the walking undoes the effect of long days sitting at work.

sections.title: Your week
sections.note: Missed a workout? Do it the next day and carry on in order. Every workout ends with a walk on the walking pad, so the walking happens on workout days too.

sections.title: Why a steady 1 kg a week
items: At about **1 kg a week**, {startKg} kg to {goalKg} kg takes about **{weeksToGoal} weeks**. Trying to go faster means eating so little that you'd lose muscle, feel drained and be far more likely to put it back on.

**The plan: about {checkpointKg} kg at the week-{checkpointWeek} checkpoint.** If the pace settles at 0.5–0.8 kg a week, that's still excellent. You'll simply reach your goal a few weeks later and be much more likely to stay there.

sections.title: How power sets work
sections.body: Each workout is built from **pairs** (A1 + A2, B1 + B2, C1 + C2). The two exercises work different muscles, so one rests while the other works. More work in less time, and your heart rate stays up the whole way through.

items: **Mobility:** 10 arm circles each way · 10 hip circles each way · 10 bodyweight squats · 10 glute bridges · 5 slow cat-cows.
**Stretch:** 30 s each for hip flexors, hamstrings, chest and a child's pose. Hip-flexor stretches matter most for anyone who sits all day.

sections.body: Same exercises all the way through. Every 3 weeks you add sets, rest a little less and walk a little longer. Check this at the start of each phase.

sections.note: In the workout tables, sets are written as **Phase 1 / Phase 2 / Phase 3**. So “3 / 4 / 4” means 3 sets in weeks 1–3, then 4 sets from week 4.

sections.title: Getting stronger with light weights
items: Every exercise has a rep range, like 12–15. Start at the bottom of it with perfect form.
Add 1–2 reps a week until you hit the **top** of the range on **every** set.

Then make it harder, one change at a time: lower for a slow count of 3 · pause 2 s at the hardest point · add ankle weights (bridges, kickbacks, leg raises) · move up a version (knee push-up to full push-up, two-leg bridge to single-leg).
Waist moves: add 5–10 s to holds or 2 reps each week.
When 5 kg feels easy on rows, presses and lunges (often around weeks 4–6), a pair of 8 kg dumbbells is a worthwhile buy.

sections.title: Your waistline: the honest version
items: No exercise can choose where fat comes off. Your waist gets smaller as your overall body fat drops, which is what the calorie counting and walking do. This plan helps your waistline in more ways:
**The waist circuit** trains the deep “corset” muscles that hold your middle in.
**Back and glute work** improves posture. Standing tall alone changes how your waist looks.
**Less bloating** from the food and water tips on the fuel page.
Measure your waist **every week**. It often moves even when the scale doesn't.

sections.title: Start safely
items: Week 1: go easy and learn the movements, especially the kettlebell swing. Soreness for 2–3 days is normal; sharp or joint pain is not, so stop that exercise. If you've had a baby in the last year, have back pain, or have any medical condition, check with your doctor or a physiotherapist before starting the core work.

sections.body: You already walk every day, which is a big advantage. Walking burns calories without making you much hungrier, helps you recover between workouts and counters long hours at a desk. Here's how to get the most from it.

sections.note: Walk-day minutes can be split up, for example 25 min before work and 25 min in the evening. It all counts.

cards.title: On the walking pad
items: Stand tall, eyes forward, arms swinging. Prop your phone or TV at eye level so you don't hunch.
Brisk means you can talk in short sentences but not sing (effort 5–6 out of 10).
Never wear ankle weights while walking. They strain knees and hips.
Comfortable trainers, not socks or slippers.

cards.title: Sitting all day? Break it up
items: Every 45–60 min of sitting, stand up and move for 2–3 min: refill water, take the stairs, stretch.
Take phone calls standing or walking.
Set a quiet reminder on your phone or watch.
Sit tall, feet flat, screen at eye level. Slouching pushes your belly out.

cards.title: Walking intervals (from week 4)
items: On walk days, add 6–8 rounds of 3 min brisk / 1 min as fast as you can walk.
This burns more than a steady walk without the impact of running.
Warm up and cool down with 5 easy minutes.

cards.title: 5-minute evening reset
items: Hip-flexor stretch, 30 s each side (kneeling lunge, tuck your hips under).
10 glute bridges to wake up your glutes after sitting.
8 slow cat-cows for your back.
Chest opener in a doorway, 30 s, then child's pose, 30 s.

sections.title: A sample walk day
sections.intro: Split it up so it fits around work. Every minute counts the same.
rows: 20 min brisk on the pad while you catch up on news or messages
10 min walk outside, even just around the block
20 min on the pad during a TV show: 4 rounds of 3 min brisk / 1 min fast from week 4
50 min and roughly 5,000–6,000 steps, before counting the rest of your day

sections.body: Counting your calories every day is the single most important habit for your goal, and you're already doing it. These tips keep the loss steady, protect your muscle and help your waist look its flattest.

cards.title: Keep doing what's working
items: Log everything honestly, including cooking oil, sauces, drinks and weekend meals.
Losing about 1 kg a week takes a gap of roughly 1,000 kcal a day between what you eat and what you burn. Daily walking and the workouts do part of that work.
Part of week one's loss is usually water. From here, **0.5–1 kg a week is a win**, and it naturally slows as you get lighter.

cards.title: For a flatter waist
items: Fill half your plate with vegetables. Fibre keeps digestion moving and you feeling full.
Drink 2–2.5 litres of water a day. It reduces water retention rather than adding to it.
Fizzy drinks, alcohol and very salty or processed food all cause bloating. Keep them occasional.
Sleep 7–8 hours. Short sleep raises hunger and cravings the next day.

cards.title: Know your floor
items: Don't go below about **1,200 kcal a day** without a doctor or dietitian.
Eating too little costs muscle, slows your progress and makes it harder to keep the weight off.
Scale stuck for 2 weeks? First check your logging, then add 1,000–2,000 steps a day, then trim 100–150 kcal. Never below the floor.

cards.title: Weighing in the smart way
items: Weigh in every morning or 3–4 times a week, after the toilet, before eating.
Log the **weekly average**. Daily numbers jump 1–2 kg with water and salt.
In the days before your period, water weight can add 1–2 kg. Compare with the same week last month.
Measure your waist every week, same time of day, relaxed, at your belly button.

cards.title: Protein: 100–120 g a day
items: Protein protects your muscle and keeps you full on fewer calories.
Aim for 25–35 g at every meal.
Easy sources: chicken, eggs, fish or tinned tuna, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, lean mince, beans and lentils, lean biltong, a protein shake.

sections.title: A sample day
sections.intro: Roughly 1,400 kcal and 110+ g protein. Adjust portions to match the number that's working for you in your app.
rows: 2 eggs, 1 slice wholegrain toast, tomato and spinach
120 g chicken breast, big salad, ½ cup cooked rice or a small wrap
170 g plain Greek yoghurt with berries
30 g lean biltong or a protein shake
150 g fish or lean mince, a plate of vegetables, a small potato

sections.body: These are general guidelines, not a medical or dietitian's plan. If you have a medical condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or take medication that affects appetite or blood sugar, check with your doctor first.

weighIn.text: Weigh in every morning or 3–4 times a week, after the toilet, before eating. The app averages each week for you.

fields.label: Waist at navel
fields.hint: Tape level at your belly button, relaxed, after breathing out.

fields.label: Waist, narrowest

steps.text: Write your step count each day, or walking-pad minutes if you don't track steps.

wins: Clothes feel looser around the waist
Waist down 3 cm from the start
First full push-up (not from the knees)
A full week of hitting the daily step target
Kettlebell swings feel easy at 15 reps

sitBreaks.text: Every 45–60 min of sitting, stand up and move for 2–3 min.

bands.message: Scale stuck for 2 weeks? First check your logging, then add **1,000–2,000 steps** a day, then trim **100–150 kcal**. Never below 1,200 kcal.
Still healthy progress. Keep logging honestly and keep your walks up. Check your waist: it often moves when the scale doesn't.
Right on track. **0.5–1 kg a week is a win.**
Great week. Make sure you're getting 100–120 g protein so the loss stays fat, not muscle.
Faster than planned. Make sure you're eating at least **1,200 kcal** and 100 g protein a day. Losing too fast costs muscle.

notes: In the days before your period, water weight can add 1–2 kg. Compare with the same week last month.
Part of week one's loss is usually water, so expect the pace to settle after that.
